newsitem.title: FRANCE: France needs single voice in Europe - Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France needs single voice in Europe - Chirac.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac, in a veiled warning to voters against electing a left-wing government, said on Tuesday that France could only defend its interests in Europe if it spoke with a single voice.

In a solemn statement to the media five days before the first round of a parliamentary election, the conservative Chirac pledged that France would meet its European commitments, a clear reference to fulfilling terms for a single European currency.

"Let us not forget that (France) will only be able to defend its interests if it is capable of speaking with a single voice, a strong voice," he said before meeting German Chancellor Helmut Kohl for talks on European Union issues.

Kohl, who was expected to give a joint news conference with Chirac later, arrived from Bonn for the latest in a series of frequent Franco-German consultations ahead of Friday's informal EU summit in the Dutch resort of Noordwijk.

The conditions for a single European currency have been a subject of debate in the campaign for the May 25-June 1 election, with the opposition Socialists and Communists ruling out further austerity to meet the budget deficit criteria.
"France will meet its European commitments with lucidity and pragmatism. With the support of the French people, I will watch over that," the president said.
"It will do so because our economy is in better shape and we have recreated the conditions for good growth," he said.
Although he did not say so explicitly, Chirac implied that a left-wing election victory, which opinion polls suggest is unlikely, would call into question the whole process of European integration.
"How can one imagine that everything that has been built for the last 40 years could be cast into doubt or put on hold without causing irreparable damage for our country," he said.
His comments echoed a warning to voters against left-right "cohabitation" made by centre-right Prime Minister Alain Juppe earlier on Tuesday.
Juppe said France's place in the single currency could be endangered if the left won the poll because of what he said were the Socialists' deficit spending plans.

"It would be a shambles in Europe, firstly because the Socialists and Communists don't agree among themselves...and also because the Socialists' economic policy, with extra spending and deficits, would push us off track for European (monetary) union," he told RTL radio.
"We have made conditions so that the euro will succeed. I rather have the feeling that (Socialist leader) Lionel Jospin is making conditions so it will fail," Juppe said.
Jospin told the newspaper Le Monde there would be no crisis over the single currency if the left won and accused the centre-right government of kowtowing to Germany.

The Socialist chief said he would not feel bound by a "stability pact", adopted by European Union leaders in Dublin last December, limiting the public deficits of countries that join the euro once it is launched in 1999.
